intervals.label: data taking
intervals.note: The official page dates data taking with the various detector types to 1987-2002. Individual instruments started later: the first imaging telescope's camera in mid-1992 and AIROBICC in 1992 (arXiv:2406.15037); the five-telescope stereoscopic system was completed in 1997.
intervals.quote: With its various types of detectors HEGRA was taking data between 1987 and 2002.

intervals.label: data taking ended
intervals.note: The Cherenkov telescopes were dismantled in September 2002 (same page).
intervals.quote: With its various types of detectors HEGRA was taking data between 1987 and 2002.

name: HEGRA air-shower and Cherenkov telescope complex
notes: The imaging telescopes were dismantled in September 2002 (official page).

placements.quote: (2200 m a.s.l., 28.750 N, 17.890 W) covering an area of about 200m · 200m

altitude.quote: at a height of 2200 m a.s.l.

energy_range.quote: The system provides a gamma-ray energy threshold around 0.5 TeV.
energy_range.value: IACT gamma-ray threshold about 0.5 TeV; spectrum of the Crab measured up to 80 TeV

mirror_area.note: Design value of the five-telescope stereoscopic system; the first telescope had a different mirror area.
mirror_area.quote: five identical telescopes with 8.5 m2 mirror area

telescope_count.quote: There were a total of six of these telescopes in operation.

description.quote: 49 of these detectors were spread in a 7-by-7 grid to observe the amplitude and the time of arrival of the front of Cherenkov light. Another 48 were added later on.
description.value: Angle-integrating Cherenkov counters: 49 detectors in a 7-by-7 grid, with 48 more added later.

description.quote: More than 250 of these counters were in operation, spread over a 180-by-180 m2 area.
description.value: More than 250 scintillation counters spread over a 180 m by 180 m area.

description.quote: Muon 'Towers' with 16 m2 area each. Seventeen of these detectors were installed on La Palma.
description.value: Seventeen muon towers of 16 m2 area each.

summary.plain: A set of detectors over an area of about 200 by 200 metres: imaging Cherenkov telescopes, light counters, ground-level scintillators and muon detectors, all watching air showers from cosmic particles.
summary.technical: Combined complex: stereoscopic IACT system (8.5 m2 mirrors, 271-pixel cameras, FoV about 4.6 deg), AIROBICC wide-angle Cherenkov counters, scintillator array, muon towers, plus CRT and CLUE.

technology.quote: It consisted of several detector types for observing secondary particles or light from particle cascades in the atmosphere (Extensive Air Showers, EAS).
technology.value: Combined air-shower complex of imaging atmospheric Cherenkov telescopes, the AIROBICC angle-integrating Cherenkov counters, a scintillator array and muon towers.
